I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Without Within 2, suite directe du premier... on y retrouve la petite Vinty qui veut toujours devenir quelqu'un! La Visual Novel laisse la place à une suite plus linéaire mais qui propose une interactivité hors jeu vraiment intéressante. Un joli voyage se profile à l'horizon, touchant, drôle. Un jeu qui chance radicalement des autres VN, en faisant l'une des plus attachantes auxquelles j'ai joué. Ne vous prenez pas la tête à savoir quelle waifu vous aller choisir, quel drame vous allez devoir surmonter, ce genre de choses... détendez-vous, profitez du voyage et marrez-vous bien! Je conseille sans hésiter.

Without Within 2 continues pretty much directly from where the first game ended, with Vinty gaining some questionable internet fame (through a viral video of her freaking out after a guy insulted her work while she was selling it on the streets) and receiving a government grant to attend a calligraphy event in Melbourne, with a chance of meeting her idol and star calligrapher Excelia. Still poor (and basically barely holding together), she departs for her first long-distance trip ever, as always plagued by unfortunate events and small disasters created by her lack of experience.

The probably most unusual feature of this game is its in-detail approach to the experience of travelling to Melbourne - it not only takes its time expressing the stress and wonder Vinty feels leaving her city and flying a place for the first time, but describes the way she commutes after arriving and the landmarks she witnesses in a manner worthy of a travel guide (including links to real-life videos showing the locations where many scenes take place). This has very little to do with the substance of the story, but it's also kind of neat, I guess (not that I'm in danger of ever having the money to visit Australia from Europe, but whatever).

When it goes to the story itself, it's slightly less a comedy about Vinty's internal struggles, as quite a lot of the focus is put on Excelia, who Vinty first meats on her flight and than have further, turbulent interactions with. She's a quite interesting counterpart to Vinty, as she both embody her every aspiration and proves to be a much more contradictory and petty character that her public image would suggest. The two complement each other quite well and form a bond of sorts during the story, but it also feels awfully rushed with how much of reading time is spent with unrelated gags and "tourist guide" stuff. Excelia's behaviour and its fallout are never really explained to a satisfying degree and that feels like a lot of lost potential - the most meaningful parts of the story are kind of glossed over. It doesn't make for a bad read, but for a strangely unbalanced one still.

While the game is definitely longer (around 2 hours of reading) and more complex than the first one (minus choices, as it's completely linear), the production quality is on similar levels. The art is silly and heavily stylized, with both it and the music creating a fun, cute experience. With its unusual themes and ideas, it's something I definitely recommend visual novel fans to check out, even with the complains I've mentioned earlier - it could've done a lot of things better and choose its priorities more consistently, but it's still an enjoyable, casual read, more or less worth the $5 asking price. And especially if you grab it on sale, you'll definitely get your money's worth out of it.

Ultimately a decent continuation of the Vinty saga, Without Within 2 was fairly good. Not quite as funny as the original in the same ways, but at the same time just as funny in other ways. 

PROS:

+ Beautiful illustrations; it's clear that Karla Featherstone (the author) has improved her skills somewhat since the first.

+ Nice, soothing music. Not to mention a much larger number of songs than the first one. 

+ Vinty is funny.

+ Vinty is cute.

+ Vinty's grandma is the best when it comes to making reviews.

+ This review was TOTALLY NOT Vinty's grandma's idea.

+ [spoiler] Excelia looks adorable with the fanged look. [/spoiler]

+ [spoiler] This one includes youtube footage of the actual city, to improve immersion. It's quite facinating, seeing the city as though walking alongside Vinty on her adventures. [/spoiler]

+ [spoiler] The "shower scene" in particular was freaking hilarious. [/spoiler]

+ The waitress in that one restraunt was AWESOME. I hope she gets more screentime in later installments, 'cuz she's awesome.

CONS:

- Certain characters' motives and backstory still remain highly unclear.

- Some sequences still don't make much sense. [spoiler] For example, the "Excelia's true face" scene. [/spoiler]

- There are NO choices in this one!! NONE. This is a kinetic novel with zero choices, and limited replayability, unlike the first one. Personally, this alone is a MAJOR con that almost made me consider making this a negative review. But all in all, I enjoyed the characters themselves enough that I'd still reccommend this story anyways.

- It's really, really short, just like the first one. I'd expect that from a free-to-read, but from a digital novel that is being sold? Disappointing.

All in all, I'd highly reccommend getting this story, but ONLY if you enjoyed the first one, and ONLY while on sale. Granted, I've made worse investments; a booster pack of cards is roughly 4$, which is slightly less than what this game costs at full price. So for the price of disappointment at not getting the cards I'm after, instead I can sink it into a short story that makes me laugh and smile for a little while. And also breakfast. 'Cuz, ya know. Being able to eat is important. 

So yeah, I don't exactly regret sinking some pocket change into this, though I am kind of disappointed at how this installment of the series failed to deliver the multiple-choice gameplay/storywriting that I've come to expect from Vinty's misadventures. And ultimately, the more I read Invert Mouse's works, the more of myself I see in them. They have a sort of friendly, earthy charm that onlt an indie dev 'can' have. And at the same time it stays true to the feel of the first one, for the most part.

TL;DR: You should totally get it, but only on sale and only if you liked the first one's true story path.

[i]WOWI2[/i] is the second game in the series as one can guess, and it continues following Vinty's journey as an aspiring calligraphy artist. This one is a lot longer compared to the first game, and contains most of your usual Steam features, like cards and achievements: but even though it bears more material, it comes a bit short in narrative quality and humor departments compared to the first game. Still, it is a cute enough game, and even if you are remotely curious about how Vinty's life turned out to continue after the first game, 5 dollars isn't that expensive to support an indie developer.

After her breakdown makes poor little Vinty an internet sensation, something actually nice happens to even out her bad luck and makes you reconsider whether there may be karma: she gets a government grant to attend a calligraphy event in Melbourne, Australia! All excited, little Vinty makes all her preparations months before the day of travel. On top of all, the same event is to be attended by Excelia, the calligrapher extraordinaire and Vinty's idol. Let's see how it all turns out, huh?

If you haven't played the first game, go ahead and spare 15 minutes of your time to do so now, 'cause it's free here on Steam. You played it? Good, now you are familiar with the art style of the series, which doesn't change at all in this one. It is very simple and comical anime art, stapled on some basic environment backgrounds. The narrative uses up all kinds of idioms and trashy pop culture references from "YOLO swag" to "you were expecting a nude, weren't you?". They bring in a smile or two in that manner.

The whole game can be divided into two things actually: a continuous love letter to the city of Melbourne and Vinty's continuous comparison of her own life to whatever she encounters in this travel – and both these parts has their problems that makes the game a bit boring. Most of the narrative in the game, from start till the end narrates Vinty walking around, exploring the city, using all kinds of vehicles like trams, trains, planes, taxis etc. and none of these scenes contain enough personal narrative or impression. She just gets excited over differences, comparing to her own hometown. It’s as if the developer has been paid a grant from the city of Melbourne for touristic advertisement. Even if that would be the issue, there are not enough narratives of landmarks to begin with. But we spare nearly an hour reading about her using all kinds of transports. Oh, and there are actual video links to developer's YouTube page, which were recorded travelling to, from and within Melbourne city to endorse immersion. Lots of work there, people! At least you are authentic.

As for the other part of the game: she compares herself to Experia, she compares Melbourne to her home town, she compares her hotel room to her apartment etc... and she continuously ends up displaying an exaggerated inferiority complex about all her comparisons. Well, she manages to overcome that inferiority at the end, but it is kinda boring to witness her insecurities and screw ups all through the game. These kinda things bear sincerity to a degree and they are relatable - as it was the issue in the first game - but here, maybe due to game being longer, they come as a bit annoying. Still, the game manages to display a point by the end to wrap up a decent enough life lesson. You just gotta wait until you get there.

Can I recommend the game? Well, not particularly as it is, but I can see there is some heart and real effort put into the game, so I really wouldn't like to give it a downvote. It is just a game that could have been way better. Consider it as a nice enough trial and a promise to make things more interesting in the future, since WOWI3 is about to hit Steam store within 2 weeks. Enjoy, people!

记得刚开始用steam的时候玩过这个的前作，是个幽默又励志的短故事来着，看到续作出了就买了，然后就一直放置忘了玩，这两天总算想起来了，稍微花了点时间玩通关。

虽说长度是前作的五倍，不过也就一个小时左右的时间就能打通，可爱的女主角玟缇这次要到墨尔本去看她偶像艾希里亚，顺便在墨尔本观光。游戏的前半部分就是流水账式的墨尔本游记（虽然还是有那种小幽默在里面），基本上每隔几句话就有一个youtube的链接，是作者拍的和剧情对应的小视频，飞机起飞啦公交车啦各种景点啦，虽然不看也完全不影响剧情，不过看了能多少营造出一点出国旅游的感觉吧（但是出现太频繁有点打断游戏体验），晚上玟缇洗澡的时候也有一个视频，当然什么也看不到（就这画风你在期待什么）。

然后第二天开始就是真正的剧情展开了。[spoiler] 玟缇去参加艾希里亚的书法活动，结果本该播放艾希里亚介绍视频的时候视频被人掉包了，播放出来的是艾希里亚涂掉其他书法家的作品，还叫人开小号在网上喷玟缇等等的恶行，在场的书法家都炸了，大家开始互相伤害毁坏别人的作品。结束之后玟缇去安慰形象崩坏而伤心的艾希里亚，还请她去平民餐馆吃饭，最后两个人成了朋友兼好对手，完。讲真这个剧情我真的无力吐槽，前面花那么多篇幅使用各种夸张的描写说艾西里亚多么有名多么优秀多么有钱，和玟缇简直云泥之别不是一个世界的人，那么这样的一个人为什么要去黑那些没名气的小书法家啦对她有什么好处吗（除非她有什么特殊的阴暗心理，尽管自己已经很成功了，还是以破坏别人的梦想为乐），最后大家闹完一通之后玟缇的反应给人感觉是她只是不小心犯了一点无伤大雅的小错误而已，艾西里亚自己也完全没有反省（是是反正全是黑你的人不好），网友也是支持她的居多，拜托如果这些都是真的的话那是人品问题好吗，可不是能用“腹黑是萌点”什么的就可以混过去的，我知道从编剧的角度来说想要把这么一位云端里的角色拉到和我们的主角同一水平，以此来让她们产生友谊，但这也太不知轻重了，什么“我们互相伤害”啊，你们名气差距那么大，她在网上黑你造成的伤害可比你毁她一幅作品大多了（要是设计揭露艾西里亚真相的是玟缇还能勉强算是“互相伤害”），不要觉得你们一起去吃了顿平民饭就变成同一阶级了啊，直到最后我还在想会不会其实那些事都是假的，是艾西里亚黑捏造的，结果并不是。作者想表达的大概就是你不要一味地崇拜别人失去自己的特色，但这个表达方法实在叫人有点难接受，就算她实力再强，也不能因此轻易原谅她人品不好，就算她人品不好，实力的差距仍然在那，玟缇想要达到她的高度并没有变得更容易，因为这事而成为朋友还很励志的下定决心要超越她有点难理解，也可能是文化差异，或者我对这种低龄向励志故事太较真了吧...	[/spoiler]

当然本作的优点还是有不少的，画风还是那么可爱，而且相比前作也能看出进步，眯眯眼的玟缇作为这个制作组的看板娘，真的是超级萌，让人好想捏捏她的脸（那些犀利的吐槽也很有趣），BGM虽然让人不太有拿出来单独听的欲望，但是放在游戏里还是比较应景的，中文翻译比起前作好了很多，虽然还是有错字，但至少没有简体版里混着繁体字这种事情了（那些小视频我其实不知道该算优点还是缺点，至少能看出作者很有爱吧，不过还是希望能做进游戏里面，我一向不太喜欢这种在游戏里放网页链接的，特别是这种放在游戏过程里的...)。

看在很可爱又支持中文的份上还是好评吧（虽然我希望这个作者的其他作品也能有中文，不过看样子可能性不大），另外我买了artbook的dlc，但是不知道为什么不能下载，ost就是正常的...
